verdict.rationale: Fellow's own docs show some least-privilege controls for agent access. Workspace admins choose which MCP tools members' AI assistants can use, MCP connections only reach data the user can already see, and owners can revoke connections and see last-used timestamps. The REST API also supports multiple named keys, with a separate key recommended per application, and broad cross-workspace access is reserved for distinct Super Admin keys. However, nothing shows that an individual API key can be limited to specific permissions, resources, or read-only access; standard keys appear to inherit the full rights of the user who created them. Missing for 10: per-key permission scopes (e.g. read-only or endpoint/resource-limited keys), key expiry/rotation controls, per-agent scoping of MCP credentials beyond the workspace-wide tool allowlist, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
